mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.3 percentage points signals improved labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the Housing Starts Index exceeding 10% indicates weakening residential demand, which reduces construction-related earnings and confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when HOUST declines by more than 10% over 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month contraction in the Industrial Production Index below -0.5% signals deteriorating manufacturing activity, which pressures earnings and risk sentiment, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% signals a tightening stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in one month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures exceeding 1% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when RSAFS falls by more than 1% over 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when UNRATE falls by more than 0.4pp and drops below 4% over 2 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 1-month increase in GDP growth above 0.5% combined with a 1-month increase in Housing Starts above 3% signals synchronized demand expansion, which boosts earnings and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline when both GDPC1 and HOUST rise by more than their respective thresholds in one month (t-test p > 0.05).
